title: Microgravity-Induced Ocular Changes: Retinal and Choroidal Vascular Alterations in Rodents
description: Longitudinal evaluation of microvascular and structural integrity of retinal and optic head tissues after 37 days aboard the International Space Station, highlighting venous engorgement and oxidative stress pathways.
relevance: Direct animal model for cephalad fluid shift and choroidal vascular congestion in microgravity.

title: Multi-Omics Profiling of Ocular and Cephalic Tissues from Spaceflight Missions
description: Comparative transcriptomic and proteomic survey examining extracellular matrix remodeling in the posterior sclera and blood-retinal barrier disruption during spaceflight.
relevance: Underpins molecular mechanisms of posterior globe flattening and biomechanical scleral stiffness.

title: Optic Nerve Sheath Diameter and Retinal Nerve Fiber Layer (RNFL) Thickness Biomarkers
description: High-resolution optical coherence tomography (OCT) tracking of peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness in bed-rest analogs and long-duration spaceflight crews.
relevance: Gold standard quantitative imaging reference for SANS Frisén staging and RNFL edema monitoring.

title: Endothelial Response to Simulated Microgravity and Elevated CO2 in Human Retinal Microvessels
description: Analysis of endothelial permeability and nitric oxide synthase expression under rotating wall vessel microgravity combined with ISS-representative ambient CO2 levels (0.4%).
relevance: Investigates environmental compounding factors (ambient spacecraft CO2) in intracranial fluid dynamics.
